_protocol: Hill-climb registry: one entry per reference track being reproduced. The live `groove` plays them in turn as a playlist (tools/playlist.py).
1. `song` is ALWAYS the best version so far. Keep experiments elsewhere (/tmp, *-wip.yaml); commit the song file only when it beats `best.score`, and update `best` in the same commit.
2. Do NOT `chirp live replace` the groove yourself. The playlist driver loads each song fresh when its turn comes, and hot-swaps the playing song at the next bar when its file changes on disk.
3. Commit to this repo (git add <your files>; git commit; git pull --rebase origin main; git push origin HEAD:main). Touch only your own entry and files; never rewrite another climb's song.

4. Every song must plan with the groove's pinned binary (tools/restart-groove.sh pins origin/main builds). A song needing newer engine features is skipped (logged in /tmp/chirp-playlist.log) until the groove restarts on a newer build.
5. `passes`: how many times the song plays per turn. `enabled: false` takes a climb out of rotation. Runtime overrides (ignored by git): tools/playlist-solo holds one id to play exclusively.

climbs.reference: DOOM: The Dark Ages OST (Finishing Move) — When The Shadows First Lengthened (menu theme), YouTube UOXI5uSPIaQ
climbs.metric: python3 tools/likeness.py sections ref/shadows.wav OUT.wav $(cat tools/shadows-sections.txt)
